label: Childbirth complication
target_basis: WHO indicator: geographic access to emergency obstetric care within 2 hours of travel time (https://www.who.int/data/gho/indicator-metadata-registry/imr-details/geographic-access-to-emergency-obstetric-care-(emoc)-health-facilities-within-2-hours-of-travel-time)

label: Snakebite
target_basis: About 2 hours is the maximum ideal time to antivenom used in accessibility studies (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8757981/); a population standard, not a clinical limit

label: Snakebite (antivenom only at district hospitals)
target_basis: Same 2 hour basis as snakebite; strict case because not every upazila hospital has antivenom

label: Injury or drowning
target_basis: Lancet Commission on Global Surgery: 2 hours to essential surgical care such as open fracture care (https://www.thelancet.com/commissions-do/global-surgery); drowning also needs first aid at the scene

label: Minor illness
target_basis: Common 60-minute primary-care access convention in accessibility studies (e.g. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12557955/); not a clinical threshold
